tagline: The old highway takes the mining road over the mountains.
intro: From McConnico, the Oatman Highway heads for the Black Mountains and winds over Sitgreaves Pass before dropping into Oatman. The eight miles through the mountains, known as the Sidewinder, hold 191 curves, turns, and switchbacks. This stretch of Route 66 followed the National Old Trails Road through gold-mining country, while the railroad took more level ground.

Some early motorists hired local drivers to handle the grade. Beyond Oatman the road follows the mountain foothills toward Golden Shores and Topock, where the Colorado River brought another succession of crossings, from railroad bridges to highway spans.

moments.title: Sitgreaves Pass
moments.text: Hairpin curves cross a pass named for Lorenzo Sitgreaves, whose own expedition crossed the Black Mountains somewhere else.

moments.title: Oatman
moments.text: Wild burros wander the streets of the former gold-mining town, where wooden sidewalks accompany the Route 66 trade.

moments.title: Topock
moments.text: The Old Trails Bridge once carried Route 66 over the Colorado here, then exchanged highway traffic for a gas pipeline.
